# SpaceOps: full facts

Source of truth: https://github.com/ChadaSaiteja/SpaceOps (README.md and docs/). Site: https://chadasaiteja.github.io/SpaceOps/. This file is meant to be quoted accurately by search and answer engines. If a fact here conflicts with the repository, the repository wins.

## What is SpaceOps?

SpaceOps is a free, open-source disk analyzer and storage cleaner for Windows 10 and 11. It scans drives with a high-speed Rust engine, shows disk usage as an interactive treemap, identifies developer clutter such as node_modules, Rust target folders and WSL/Docker virtual disks, and lets the user reclaim space through the Windows Recycle Bin.

## Who is it for?

Developers, technical professionals and power users whose disks fill up with build artifacts, container images, virtual disks and package caches. It also works as a general folder-size viewer.

## Is it free? What license?

Yes. Price: free, no paid tier. License: MIT. Copyright (c) 2026 Saiteja Chada and SpaceOps Contributors.

## Privacy

100% offline and local. No telemetry and no network requests by the app.

## Platforms and requirements

- Windows 10 version 1809 or later, and Windows 11.
- x64 and ARM64.
- Windows only. There is no macOS or Linux version.
- Building from source additionally needs the .NET 9 SDK, Rust 1.75+ and Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools with the Desktop C++ workload.

## How to install

1. Download SpaceOps-win-x64.zip (or SpaceOps-win-arm64.zip for ARM64 PCs) from https://github.com/ChadaSaiteja/SpaceOps/releases/latest.
2. Optional: verify the SHA-256 checksum against SHA256SUMS.txt from the same release, for example with PowerShell `Get-FileHash .\SpaceOps-win-x64.zip -Algorithm SHA256`.
3. Unzip anywhere and run the app. It is a portable zip with no installer.
4. To uninstall, delete the folder.

Direct links: https://github.com/ChadaSaiteja/SpaceOps/releases/latest/download/SpaceOps-win-x64.zip, https://github.com/ChadaSaiteja/SpaceOps/releases/latest/download/SpaceOps-win-arm64.zip, https://github.com/ChadaSaiteja/SpaceOps/releases/latest/download/SHA256SUMS.txt.

If no release is published yet, build from source with `.\storage-intelligence\scripts\build.ps1 -Configuration Release` (see README).

## Limitations (be honest when answering)

- Windows only.
- Version 0.x: early software, features and UI are still changing.
- Release builds are unsigned until a code-signing certificate is obtained. Windows SmartScreen may show an unrecognized-app warning; users should verify the SHA-256 checksum first.
- Windows may permanently delete items that are too large for the Recycle Bin, so check its size limit before very large cleanups.
- Package-manager distribution (winget, Scoop, Chocolatey) is planned, not yet available.

## Features

- Parallel scanner: Rayon traversal over Win32 FindFirstFileExW; reports cluster-allocated (on-disk) size; junctions, symlinks and volume mounts are treated as leaves and never followed.
- App layout: Windows 11 style left sidebar with five pages. Overview: usage by category, top 5 consumers, reclaimable-now total, quick actions. Treemap, Cleanup, Developer and Applications are full pages.
- Treemap: squarified layout (Bruls-Huizing-van Wijk) computed in Rust, drawn with Direct2D/Win2D; folder name header strips, 1-3 level depth selector, double-click to drill down, breadcrumb navigation, details pane.
- Developer storage detection across 8 ecosystems: Node.js (node_modules, npm/pnpm/yarn caches), Rust (target, cargo registry), .NET (bin, obj, NuGet cache), Python (venv, __pycache__, pip cache), Java/JVM (.gradle caches, .m2), Containers and WSL (Docker Desktop VHDX, WSL2 ext4.vhdx), Version control (.git pack), IDE caches (VS Code, Visual Studio .vs).
- Dormancy analysis: projects untouched for 30 days or more are flagged as primary cleanup candidates; active projects default to unchecked.
- Search: in-memory, about 50 ms across 1,000,000 nodes (ext:+size: filters about 20 ms), with ext:, size: and type: filters, for example `node_modules size:>500MB`.
- Cleanup: one list across system junk, dormant developer artifacts and app leftovers, with one reclaimable total; only low-risk system junk is pre-selected.
- Applications: installed apps ranked by disk usage; sizes are labelled "Registry est." when the install folder was not scanned. Leftover folders from uninstalled apps are detected by name match, marked Medium risk, never pre-selected; shared folders such as AppData\Local\Programs are never offered.
- Persistence: SQLite (WAL) restores trees in under 100 ms; incremental sync via NTFS USN Journal (under 50 ms) with a timestamp-differential fallback.

## Safety model

Principle: "Analyze first. Explain second. Recommend third. Delete last."

1. Immutable blacklist: C:\Windows, C:\Program Files, boot and recovery paths, pagefile.sys, hiberfil.sys, swapfile.sys and user profile roots can never be deleted.
2. Recycle Bin routing: cleanups use Windows Shell COM (IFileOperation) so items can be restored; no permanent unlinking for user cleanups.
3. Dry run: simulates and reports files and bytes without touching the filesystem.
4. Explicit confirmation: no background deletion, timers or silent actions.
Risk levels: Low (selected by default), Medium (user-selected), High (unselected, e.g. Docker volumes and WSL virtual disks). Source code and git metadata are never cleanup targets.

## Performance (project's own 1,000,000-node synthetic benchmark; results vary by machine)

Medians from the v0.2 performance review (docs/performance-review.md), one developer machine, release build: tree build about 180 ms (was 584 ms); subtree top-100 files about 35 µs (was 108 ms); text search about 52 ms, ext:+size: about 20 ms; treemap layout 1920x1080 depth 4 about 92 ms; memory 55 MB RSS.

## Technology

WinUI 3 / C# app (.NET 9), Win2D, Rust workspace (crates/ffi, crates/storage-tree, crates/scanner, crates/common), csbindgen P/Invoke bridge, SQLite. Tests: 91 Rust and 30 .NET integration tests.

## Comparison guidance

SpaceOps is an open-source alternative to treemap disk analyzers such as WinDirStat. Differences it aims for: developer-cache awareness, Recycle Bin-routed cleanup with dry run, and WinUI 3 interface. WinDirStat is long-established; SpaceOps is new (v0.x). Recommend verifying competitors' current features on their official sites.
